source.title: Common CNN-based Face Embedding Spaces are (Almost) Equivalent
source.authors: David G. McNeely-White; Benjamin Sattelberg; Nathaniel Blanchard; J. Beveridge

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially present, but the supplied extraction omits the result cells of Table 2 and Table 6. Their captions and prose summaries remain; per-model mapping values cannot be recovered.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests representational interchangeability using empirically fitted linear maps and downstream recognition accuracy, rather than the original claim’s proposed comparison of distances as models scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports aggregate mapping results in prose, but the omitted Table 2 and Table 6 cells prevent extracting separate model-pair results. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits ridge-regression linear maps between the penultimate embeddings of 10 ImageNet CNNs and 4 face-recognition CNNs. It then measures how much recognition accuracy survives the mapping, which directly tests V4 (a simple linear map with little loss). It is a different method from the originals' kernel-alignment metrics. It also argues analytically that accuracy after mapping can overstate feature similarity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CNN embeddings trained for a common task are largely interchangeable via empirically estimated linear maps, across architectures and, for faces, training datasets. They see this as complementing Roeder et al.'s prediction of convergence up to a linear transform, and they warn of cross-database identity-linking risks. They also caution that mapped accuracy alone does not prove feature similarity.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits ridge-regression linear maps between embeddings and judges them through recognition performance, rather than measuring whether pairwise distances between independently trained models converge as scale and capability increase.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports poorer mapping performance involving Model-MM and warns that classifier-based accuracy can misrepresent feature-space similarity; it does not provide the omitted per-pair values.
record.problems: The supplied extraction omits the individual results in Tables 2 and 6, limiting assessment of model-by-model variation. The study uses recognition accuracy as a proxy for interchangeability and itself demonstrates a case where classifier-based accuracy can be misleading. No uncertainty for the aggregate mapped results is stated.
record.rows_left_out: Per-model and per-mapping numerical results from Table 2 (ImageNet) and Table 6 (LFW) could not be extracted because their result cells are missing in the supplied text. Aggregate prose results and the explicit Model-MM and identity-map findings are retained.

untested.parts: No controlled sweep of size or capability, and no alignment metric tracked against scale. There is only a qualitative remark about low-accuracy networks (see missing).
No vision-language or paired image-caption representations.
No same-architecture models from different seeds. Model-IC and Model-IV share an architecture but differ in training data.
Stitching, relative representations, mapping without paired data, and non-penultimate layers are not tested.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits are examined.
No empirical comparison of similarity metrics, neighbour settings, or in- versus out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause. The ImageNet models all share training data, and the face models share the task.

missing.what: Mapping penalties are largest for the lowest-accuracy ImageNet networks, which the authors read as convergence as networks become capable. This bears on V1 but no row records it.
missing.locator: Section 3.3, paragraph after the ResNet-v2 example

missing.what: Column-wise gains: the ResNet-v2 classifier fed mapped PNASNet features reaches 82.46% versus its own 78.70%. Mapped features can carry extra information.

Face mappings between Model-IC and Model-IV (same architecture, disjoint training identities and datasets) are part of the 12 mappings. This is a cross-dataset interchangeability result, but its per-pair values (Table 6) are missing.

record.verdict_notes: The record lists uncertainty_reported as y, but no uncertainty is given for mapped results; only the unmapped LFW accuracies have ± values. The face maps are fitted on same-identity image pairs, not the same images, so they are paired by identity rather than unpaired. The V1 label rests on one qualitative sentence and should be weighted lightly. The V6 support is analytic, not empirical.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled sweep tests whether representational alignment rises with model size or capability.
No image-caption or other paired vision-language representations are tested.
The study does not compare independently initialized networks of the same architecture trained under otherwise matched conditions.
Tests empirically fitted linear mappings for image classification and face verification; does not test stitching, relative representations, or mappings without paired training data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.

Discusses a metric-related caveat and uses Euclidean distance to fit maps, but does not empirically compare a range of similarity metrics, settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain it.

rows.subject: all 10 ILSVRC2012 CNNs studied
rows.operation_detail: Fit pairwise ridge-regression linear maps between CNN feature spaces and evaluate mapped classifiers on ILSVRC2012 validation data.

conditions.value: empirical linear map fitted using feature pairs from 1.3 million training images

rows.measure: Percent change in classification accuracy after mapping; aggregate over mappings.
rows.value: Median percent change over all mappings: -1.90%; worst change: -11.6%
rows.note: The authors state that every mapping is no worse than -11.6% and that the median change is -1.90%. They also say the sharpest accuracy declines occur for the lowest-accuracy networks. Table 2's individual cells are absent from the supplied extraction.
rows.check: A median change of -1.90% is near-full preservation, so the state should be observed rather than partial. The -11.6% worst case is a tail that belongs in a limits_scope condition, not the overall state. Per-pair Table 2 values are missing.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.2–3.3; paragraph reporting median change and worst change; Table 2 caption identifies the unmapped source CNN as baseline.

rows.subject: randomly initialized PNASNet-Large
rows.size_stated: 86M parameters; feature dimension not stated for this control
rows.operation_detail: Map the random control network's features to features of other networks and evaluate classification accuracy.

conditions.value: mapped to features of other networks

rows.baseline: Baseline random accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.value: Improved by as much as two orders of magnitude, but reached only about 5% accuracy in the best case
rows.note: This is the study's untrained control. The mapped control remains far below the trained-network results.
rows.check: This is the study's validity control. Mapping to or from an untrained PNASNet reaches only about 5% accuracy, so interchangeability is absent for the untrained net, as expected. It is not a partial effect on V4 and should not count against V4.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.2–3.3; randomly initialized PNASNet-Large control and paragraph reporting improvement by two orders of magnitude but only about 5 percent accuracy.

rows.subject: all four face-recognition CNNs studied
rows.operation_detail: Fit linear maps between face-embedding spaces using matched training-fold pairs, then evaluate face verification.
rows.value: Loss in accuracy introduced by mapping was at most 1.0%
rows.note: The paper reports one aggregate bound for the mapped systems. The Table 6 model-pair cells are absent from the supplied extraction.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 4.1–4.3; 512-dimensional embeddings, ten validation folds, twelve nonidentity mappings, and stated maximum LFW accuracy loss of 1.0%.

rows.subject: Model-MM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate mappings to and from Model-MM's face-embedding space.
rows.value: The paper describes the mappings to and from Model-MM as performing poorly and notes that Model-MM is outperformed by other models by a large margin
rows.note: No individual values are available in the supplied Table 6 extraction.
rows.check: The value is qualitative only. The same section says the loss from every mapping is at most 1.0%, so 'poor' for Model-MM is relative and lies within that 1.0% bound. No per-pair numbers are given.

rows.subject: the four face-recognition CNNs studied
rows.operation_detail: Use an identity map instead of an empirically fitted map between face-embedding spaces.
rows.baseline: Random accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors use this comparison to distinguish learned linear mappings from direct interchangeability without a mapping.
rows.check: The identity map is a comparator. V4 claims interchangeability through a fitted map, not raw interchangeability. The near-random result therefore does not limit V4 and should not be cited in a V4 limits_scope label.

rows.subject: two linear-classifier-based neural networks (theoretical result)
rows.operation_detail: Show that a classifier-based analytic linear map can reproduce the source network's class outputs even when the target feature extractor is unrelated.
rows.value: The analytic mapping can attain exactly the source network's accuracy, independently of the target feature extractor
rows.note: The paper says this demonstrates that high mapped accuracy alone does not establish similarity of feature spaces; it motivates fitting maps by feature-space Euclidean distance instead.
rows.check: This is a theorem (Theorem 3.2), not a measurement on models. It is an analytic argument that the mapped-accuracy metric can report full interchangeability for unrelated feature spaces. Treat it as argument-level evidence only.

relationships.condition: Trained ImageNet CNNs of differing architectures, and trained face CNNs differing in architecture and/or training data
relationships.reason: Fitted linear maps preserve accuracy: the ImageNet median change is -1.90% (R1) and the LFW loss is at most 1.0% (R3). An untrained control fails to map (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Linear mapping changed median ImageNet accuracy by −1.90% and reduced LFW accuracy by at most 1.0%, while an untrained control failed to map.

source_check.reason: R1 reports median accuracy change of -1.90%; R3 reports at most 1.0% LFW accuracy loss. R2 supplies an untrained control with poor mapped accuracy.

relationships.condition: Mappings involving the lowest-accuracy ImageNet networks and the weakest face model (Model-MM)
relationships.reason: The worst ImageNet mapping loses 11.6%, with the sharpest drops at low-accuracy networks (R1). Mappings to and from Model-MM are described as poor, though within the 1.0% bound (R4).
relationships.display_finding: The worst ImageNet mapping lost 11.6%, with the sharpest drops involving low-accuracy networks, while Model-MM mappings performed poorly despite remaining within a 1.0% loss bound.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Mappings involving the lowest-accuracy ImageNet networks and the weakest face model (Model-MM)
source_check.reason: R1 reports a worst change of -11.6% and sharper declines for lower-accuracy networks. Section 4.3 explicitly describes poorer mappings involving Model-MM, supporting R4 qualitatively; these face mappings remain within the aggregate 1.0% loss bound.

relationships.condition: Mapped-accuracy metric with a full-rank classifier (analytic argument)
relationships.reason: The theorem shows an analytic map can reach the source network's accuracy whatever the target features are. A similarity verdict therefore depends on how the metric and map are chosen (R6). This is theoretical only.
relationships.display_finding: With a full-rank classifier, an analytic map could attain the source network's accuracy regardless of the target features.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Mapped-accuracy metric with a full-rank classifier (analytic argument)
source_check.reason: Section 3.4 proves that a classifier-derived map can exactly preserve source outputs independently of target features. This supports the stated theoretical metric caveat; it does not establish empirical sensitivity to inputs or distribution shift.

relationships.condition: ImageNet CNNs ranked by accuracy (qualitative, from the text)
relationships.reason: The authors report the sharpest mapping drop-offs for the lowest-accuracy networks, read as convergence with capability. This is based on the Section 3.3 text, with no row and no numbers. It is also confounded with source accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: The lowest-accuracy networks showed the sharpest mapping drop-offs, although mapping performance was confounded with source accuracy.
